summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including chronic lymphedema, morbid obesity, and recurrent cellulitis was admitted due to disseminated shingles and right leg cellulitis. She presented with a left-sided dermatomal rash and worsening leg swelling. Initial treatment included IV acyclovir and clindamycin. New lesions in non-adjacent dermatomes confirmed disseminated zoster, prompting a full 10-day IV antiviral course. Cellulitis improved after switching back to clindamycin from Keflex. A painful tongue lesion was evaluated by ENT and deemed a likely traumatic ulcer, not malignancy. Her chronic edema worsened with IV fluids, leading to blistering; wound care was initiated. Diuretics were restarted, and pain was managed with oral narcotics. Infectious workup showed no immunodeficiency. She was discharged home with services, on a stable medication regimen, with follow-up plans for INR monitoring, ENT evaluation, and skin care.
problems: Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
Personal history of other venous thrombosis and embolism
Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus
